strings.name: Kazuo Ishiguro
strings.role: Novelist and screenwriter · Memory and self-understanding
strings.summary: Born in Nagasaki and raised in Britain, Ishiguro writes English-language fiction about memory, responsibility and self-deception. The Remains of the Day places a butler’s recollections against historical failure; Never Let Me Go and Klara and the Sun revisit such concerns in worlds reshaped by technology. His restrained narrators gradually reveal truths they struggle to acknowledge. He received the 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature.

strings.influence.rationale: Explored memory, responsibility and identity in novels including The Remains of the Day and Never Let Me Go, advancing intercultural expression in English-language literature.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Memory and moral blind spots
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The Remains of the Day uses the butler Stevens’s recollections to examine professional loyalty and historical responsibility.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Human value across genres
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Never Let Me Go and Klara and the Sun use speculative settings to examine care, love and human value.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses the adaptation of A Pale View of Hills
strings.timeline.event-01.text: An interview revisited his first novel, family memories of war and the need for film adaptations to develop their own imagination.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes Klara and the Sun
strings.timeline.event-02.text: An artificial friend’s observations explore care, solitude and love, extending his interest in human life under technological change.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the Nobel Prize in Literature
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The Swedish Academy recognized his exploration of human connections and their illusions, bringing renewed international attention.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Never Let Me Go
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Recollections of boarding school gradually disclose lives constrained by an institution, combining coming-of-age fiction with speculation.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: The Remains of the Day wins the Booker
strings.timeline.event-05.text: A British butler’s limited perspective examines loyalty, loss and responsibility in one of his defining novels.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Publishes A Pale View of Hills
strings.timeline.event-06.text: A Japanese woman living in Britain revisits Nagasaki, beginning his sustained use of uncertain memory as a narrative structure.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Completes graduate study in creative writing
strings.timeline.event-07.text: He completed an MA at the University of East Anglia after studying English and philosophy at Kent.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Moves to Britain with his family
strings.timeline.event-08.text: His father’s oceanographic research brought the family to Surrey, a move that shaped his relationship to cultural memory.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Nagasaki
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Nagasaki, Japan; early experiences and family memories of Japan later informed his fiction.
